description.narrative:
The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT) is a non-profit international agricultural research organization that conducts research to develop innovative solutions for the drylands, dedicated to uplifting smallholder farmers andensuring food security in semi-arid tropics.
ICRISAT’s work in West and Central Africa is deeply intertwined with strengthening livelihoods, resilience, and production systems to address pressing food and nutrition requirements, combat land degradation, mitigateclimate variability, and tackle related shocks.
The role of ICRISAT in the Crop Diversity program is to support the farmer’ communities with advice and seeds, specifically:
1. Capacity strengthening of and support to farmers in Farmer Field Schools (FFS) on crop diversity 2. Supporting Business Development Initiatives from FFS and ensure the sustainability and economic viability of seed production 3. Support Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) to track progress and refine interventions
The project aims to support small-holders farmers in Mali and Nigeria facing cascading crisis of insecurity, climate change and biodiversity loss. The projectfocuses on locations that are highly vulnerable, remote, heavily affected by climate change and violent conflicts, and people oftenstruggle to cover basic needs, which leads to dependency on emergency aid. The project will work with both men and women farmers, with particular focus on engaging young farmers. Through this project an estimated 1200 smallholder farmers will be supported directly, while benefiting approximately 10,000 households indirectly. Between 40 percent of participating farmers will be women, and 20 percent youth. For smallholder farmers, seed is the most fundamental resource, access to high-quality, diverse seeds is essential for: - Enhancing crop productivity and agricultural biodiversity - Improving food and nutrition security - Strengthening resilience to climate change - Ensuring livelihood continuity season after season By engaging farmers in seed production at community level the project provides sustainable access to good-quality diverse seeds for enhanced agricultural productivity, food and nutrition security. Project activities and outcomes are: - Improved seed supply in project sites through community level seed production - Providing a diversity of crops and varieties to farmers to enable them to cope better with climate change. - Livelihood diversification resultingin increased household income for farmers in Mali and Nigeria. - Well trained and competent small-scale seed entrepreneurs including women and youth - Linkages with seed value chain actors (to the extent possible in fragile contexts) - Customize the Farmer Field School training material - Reduced dependency on seed aid within the community - Advocate for local farmers to be seed suppliers of choice where seed aid cannot be avoided. - And ultimately foster the much-needed social cohesion in the context of unrest through meeting the essential need for food in a setting that fosters collaboration and working in solidarity.

participating-org.narrative:
The International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics (ICRISAT)stands as the premier drylands agricultural research institute, dedicated to uplifting smallholder farmers and ensuring food security in semi-arid tropics. ICRISAT has strong and enduring partnerships with governments, research institutions, development agencies, and the private sector amplifies their impact, expediting agricultural transformation
ICRISAT recognizes that the significance of the dryland crops in which it specializes will be further accentuated due to the impact of climate change. Drawing from five decades of expertise, their research will continue to focus on crops vital to dryland communities, ranging from chickpea, pigeonpea, and groundnut to sorghum, pearl millet, finger millet, smallmillet, and oilseeds. ICRISAT’s mission is to reduce poverty, hunger, malnutrition and environmental degradation in the dryland tropics and to improve the productivity, profitability, and resilience of smallholder farmers. It does so by developing and disseminating climate-smart agricultural technologies, innovative farming practices, and high-yielding crop varieties. ICRISAT also equips farmers with the tools and knowledge to enhance their agricultural productivity and generate sustainable incomes. It promotes market-oriented approaches, facilitating access to markets, value chains, and entrepreneurship opportunities for smallholder farmers, thus increasing their economic opportunities and reducing their vulnerability to poverty. By empowering farmers to build resilience, diversify their income sources, and improve their overall economic well-being, ICRISAT's work plays a vital role in overcoming poverty and creating pathways to sustainable development in the dryland regions.
ICRISAT is committed to championing gender equality and socialinclusion in its work towards agricultural development. Recognizing that women play a vital role in agriculture and rural communities, ICRISAT promotes gender-responsive research and interventions to ensure that women have equal access to resources, knowledge, and decision-making processes.
By empowering women farmers through training, capacity building, and access to credit and markets, ICRISAT helps enhance their productivity, income, and overall well-being. Additionally, ICRISAT works towards social inclusion by addressing the needs of marginalized and vulnerable groups, such as smallholder farmers, indigenous communities, and youth. By facilitating meaningful participation in agricultural value chains and providing them with tailored and sustainable support, ICRISAT contributes to reducing social inequalities and promoting holistic and inclusive agricultural development.
